item.title: Lyapunov stability of polynomial vector fields is undecidable
item.description:
Milan Korda
We show that there are integers $N$ and odd $D$ such that no algorithm can decide, from the rational coefficients of a homogeneous polynomial vector field F of degree $D$ in dimension $N$, whether the origin is Lyapunov stable for $\dot Y=F(Y)$. This proves, for some large and unoptimized dimension and degree, a conjecture of V. I. Arnold.

A robot that fails at a task faces the first decision in corrective dialogue: act on its own diagnosis, consult another onboard sensor, or interrupt a person. Choosing well requires knowing how much the robot's sensors reveal about the cause and how reliable the robot's own diagnosis is.
